adds.rationale: AMD's June 13, 2023 Data Center and AI Technology Premiere unveiled the Instinct MI300X with 192GB HBM3 aimed squarely at large-language-model training/inference, positioning AMD as a credible second-source GPU vendor just as the AI buildout wave (already the portfolio's dominant thesis via NVDA) broadens beyond a single supplier.

news_evidence.summary: AMD unveils Instinct MI300X accelerator with 192GB HBM3, 5.2TB/s bandwidth, positioned for generative-AI training and inference; sampling Q3, launch Q4 2023
AMD announces it will showcase next-generation data center and AI technology at a June 13 livestream event, teasing the Instinct MI300 series ahead of the reveal

rationale_overall: No thesis breaches surfaced across the current 14-name watchlist this quarter: Rocket Lab kept launching (HASTE debut, TROPICS cubesats), IonQ hit its Forte milestone and raised revenue guidance, General Dynamics posted solid backlog growth, and NuScale/Frontline/Rockwell/Intuitive Surgical/Lockheed/ITA showed no adverse news in the trailing quarter — so no removes. The one addition, AMD, reflects the dominant AI wave entering its broadening/surge phase: a second major silicon vendor (beyond NVDA) unveiled a shipping-ready large-model accelerator in June 2023, evidence the AI buildout is deepening rather than cresting. Rejected SMCI as an AI-server add because its only news inside the lookback window was an April 24, 2023 guidance miss; its subsequent guidance raise falls after the as-of-date. Net effect: watchlist grows from 14 to 15, AI bucket goes from 1 to 2 names, well within the wave-diversity guardrail.
